title: Swahili Peanut Soup
community: Coastal and central Tanzania — the coastal peanut soup
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Swahili Peanut Soup — a thick, creamy peanut and tomato soup with Zanzibar spices, fresh coriander, and a coconut milk finish. Rich, nourishing, and deeply satisfying — the coastal marriage of inland peanut tradition and coastal coconut.
longDesc: Peanut soup with coconut milk is the coastal Tanzanian hybrid — the inland groundnut tradition meets the coastal coconut pantry. The result is richer than either alone — the peanut and coconut fats combine to produce a soup of extraordinary body.
ingredients: ½ cup raw peanuts — roasted and ground (or 4 tbsp peanut butter)
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, spices, tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes.
Whisk peanut paste with ½ cup warm water. Add to soup.
Simmer 12 minutes until thick and well flavoured.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 5 minutes.
Blend partially for a creamier texture if desired.
chefTips: Whisk peanut paste with warm water first.
Never boil after coconut milk is added.
Partial blending produces the best texture.
cookingScience: See TZA049 for peanut sauce cooking science.
reheating: Gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Rich in niacin and vitamin E.
culturalNote: Peanut soup with coconut milk is the taste of the meeting between inland and coast — the two great Tanzanian flavour traditions combining into one remarkable bowl.
